blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

items.t: The guide page is headed "Salmon River, Langley Guide | Acreages, Farms & Wells" (written October 9, 2026), with a "Homes for sale in Salmon River" section described on the page as "Live MLS® listings, updated daily"; the guide page displays no total result count, and the cards visible at reading are a snapshot only. The cards visible are labelled "Salmon River, Langley" and are mostly rural houses, plus one vacant-land card and the out-of-scope Langley City condo card flagged in the header block. The exact MLS feed filter criteria behind the guide page, and why that condo card is labelled Salmon River in it, are UNVERIFIED.

Identity: the guide covers the board sub-area "Salmon River" in the Township of Langley — a rural acreage and farm district named for the Salmon River, which runs north to the Fraser River at Fort Langley. "Salmon River" is the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board sub-area name as used in the SnapStats FVR September 2026 report; the board sub-area code is UNVERIFIED. Boundaries: the district follows the Salmon River valley between 232 Street and 264 Street, from the Fraser River side south toward 40 Avenue, with Rawlison Crescent and 56 Avenue on the upland side; no Township-published boundary for the sub-area was confirmed, so the exact Township boundary is UNVERIFIED. Nearby areas: Fort Langley to the north, Otter District to the south, Walnut Grove to the west, Aldergrove to the southeast; the guide page also names Murrayville to the southwest.
Supply shape: effectively all detached — all 5 of the sub-area's September sales were detached. Per-sub-area median prices are NOT published: UNVERIFIED.

Where the condo stock concentrates: there is none to concentrate. There are no condo streets in this district: the roads are valley farm roads and upland acreage roads (56 Avenue, Rawlison Crescent, 232 Street, 240 Street, River Road / Glover Road toward Fort Langley), and the Township's development applications route named no condo or townhome project inside the district when the area research checked it.

Poppy Secondary, 23752 52 Ave, Langley; North Otter Elementary, 5370 248 St, Langley. Catchments are address-based: for the sample address 4452 256 Street, the SD35 School Locator returns Elementary — North Otter Elementary; Middle — none shown by the locator; Secondary — D.W. Poppy Secondary; other addresses in the sub-area may fall in different catchments, and no home is promised a specific school. No SD35 school physically inside the Salmon River valley itself was confirmed: UNVERIFIED.

Transit and roads: TransLink route 562 (Walnut Grove / Langley Centre) runs on Glover Road via 96 Avenue, 88 Avenue and 202 Street to Carvolth Exchange, serving the Fort Langley edge of the district; no TransLink route was confirmed on 56 Avenue, Rawlison Crescent or the valley roads inside the district. Highway 1 access is south via the 200 Street or 232 Street interchanges; there is no SkyTrain or West Coast Express station in the district.

The Salmon River valley is Fraser River floodplain land — the Township states the Salmon River Pump Station was originally built to help mitigate flooding of the surrounding agricultural lands during freshet, provides flood protection when Fraser River levels rise, and has flood box gates that close as river levels rise; the Pump Station Upgrades are a live Township project, with Council having authorized staff to proceed with detailed design and tendering. Parcel-level floodplain mapping and watercourse setback distances: UNVERIFIED. No recreation centre or library branch inside the district was confirmed: UNVERIFIED. Health care: Langley Memorial Hospital, 22051 Fraser Highway, Langley (24/7 emergency), southwest of the district, and the Langley Urgent and Primary Care Centre at 202 - 20434 64th Avenue, Langley; a hospital or clinic inside the district is UNVERIFIED.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Salmon River Guide

items.t: Township zoning and SSMUH — Bylaw 6020: rural land is under Township of Langley Zoning Bylaw No. 2500 (the district's farm and acreage homes sit in the rural zones, including RU-2; the RU-2 minimum lot area and frontage were not confirmed from a readable bylaw section: UNVERIFIED; zone assignments for a parcel come from the bylaw Map Schedules through the Township's GeoSource). The Township's SSMUH rules under Bylaw 6020, adopted November 18, 2024, allow 3 units on eligible lots of 280 m² or smaller and 4 units on larger eligible lots up to 4,050 m², with lots over 4,050 m² ineligible for the multi-unit tiers and NO 6-plex tier in the Township; on lots larger than 4,050 m² the rules allow one secondary suite or one accessory dwelling unit in addition to the primary unit, depending on zoning. The Township caps a secondary suite at 120 m² maximum gross floor area (Bylaw No. 2500, s. 102). In Bylaw 2500, s. 102, a "coach house" is an accessory dwelling unit located only within the second storey of a detached garage — a fee-simple second unit under the zoning bylaw, never strata. On Salmon River acreages, that suite/accessory route — not a strata condo building — is the added-unit route the rules describe.

items.t: (2) A feed card outside the guide's stated rural scope — a Langley City condo unit at Cornerstone North by Marcon is labelled "Salmon River" and surfaces inside a guide whose own copy is about acreages, farms and wells.

The pump station is a live capital project. Council has authorized staff to proceed with detailed design and tendering for the Salmon River Pump Station Upgrades — flood infrastructure, not strata infrastructure, is the district's active construction story, and flood status drives insurance and lending on valley parcels.

Wells and septic are the district's "strata documents." Rural properties may use wells searchable in the provincial GWELLS database (well reports due within 90 days of work on a well), and Fraser Health's authorized-person filings are the paper trail for an onsite sewerage system. Those filings are the paper trail a buyer here actually reviews.
The neighbouring district is not a proxy, in either direction.

items.t: Salmon River is a Township of Langley rural district along the Salmon River in the township's northwest, north of the Otter area and south of Fort Langley; "Salmon River" is also the Fraser Valley board sub-area name used in the SnapStats FVR report. No Township-published boundary for the sub-area was confirmed.

The district follows the Salmon River valley between 232 Street and 264 Street, from the Fraser River side south toward 40 Avenue, with Rawlison Crescent and 56 Avenue on the upland side; main roads are 56 Avenue and Rawlison Crescent on the upland, 232 Street and 240 Street as the north–south edges, and River Road / Glover Road toward Fort Langley, with Highway 1 access south via the 200 Street or 232 Street interchanges.

Transit: TransLink route 562 (Walnut Grove / Langley Centre) runs on Glover Road at the Fort Langley edge of the district; no TransLink route was confirmed on 56 Avenue, Rawlison Crescent or the valley roads, and there is no SkyTrain or West Coast Express station in the district.

Schools: SD35 catchments are address-based. For the sample address 4452 256 Street, the SD35 School Locator returns North Otter Elementary and D.W. Poppy Secondary, with no middle school shown; Coghlan Fundamental Elementary, 4452 256 Street, is a district school of choice on the upland east side, its position inside this board sub-area not confirmed. No SD35 school physically inside the Salmon River valley itself was confirmed.

Flood: the valley is Fraser River floodplain land — the Township states the Salmon River Pump Station was built to mitigate flooding of the surrounding agricultural lands during freshet, provides flood protection when Fraser River levels rise, has flood box gates that close as river levels rise, and is in detailed design and tendering for upgrades Council authorized.

Parent community (Langley combined) attached median is $611,000 — a Langley-wide combined condo+towhome figure, never a Salmon River townhome figure; the report publishes no Salmon River–specific median.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Salmon River

items.t: The governing fact for this sub-area: there is no townhouse strata stock to apply strata diligence to: Most Salmon River properties are non-strata freehold acreages; where a strata parcel exists, BC strata law is the Strata Property Act and strata disputes go to the Civil Resolution Tribunal. A buyer told a valley property is a "townhouse" should verify title form first — on the verified record here, it will be a freehold acreage house.

ALR stratification bar: an ALR residence cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09, s.6; Strata Property Act s.239; Agricultural Land Commission Act s.21(1)). Farm land in the valley is in the Agricultural Land Reserve in places — confirm a specific parcel on the ALC maps — and that bar is the structural reason townhouse strata do not appear on ALR valley land.

ALC residence caps: principal residence at most 500 m²; suite within the principal residence only; one additional residence at most 90 m² on properties of 40 ha or less and at most 186 m² over 40 ha, subject to Township bylaws. Farm-class thresholds in full three-tier form: $2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 plus 5% of land value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by October 31 — a flat "$2,500+" statement is an error.

Township of Langley zoning and SSMUH: rural land is under Zoning Bylaw No. 2500 (farm and acreage homes sit in the rural zones, including RU-2; the RU-2 minimum lot area and frontage were not confirmed from a readable bylaw section — UNCONFIRMED). The Township Official Community Plan and the Rural Plan govern the district.

Strata standard block (applies only if a genuine strata parcel is ever verified here): Form B diligence (Strata Property Act s.59 — fees, amounts owing, approved levies, CRF balance, insurance summary, with rules, budget, Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page); depreciation reports every five years for 5+ lot stratas since July 1, 2024; CRF minimum 10% of the operating budget since Nov 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws VOID since Nov 24, 2022 (flag any directory "rentals not allowed" line void in-entry); only 55+ age bylaws valid (SPA ss.123.1/123.2, Regulation 7.01 exemptions expanded May 1, 2023).

Watercourse setbacks: the Salmon River is a salmon-bearing watercourse, so setbacks and riparian rules can limit building envelopes near the river — parcel-level setback distances for a specific parcel: UNCONFIRMED; check with the Township before planning a build.

: FTHB GST rebate — Bill C-4, Royal Assent March 13, 2026 per CRA News No. 122 (100% of GST to $1M, phasing to $1.5M, maximum $50,000, agreements Mar 20, 2025–2031); New Housing Rebate 36% / maximum $6,300 / $350K–$450K; PTT with the first-time buyer exemption (first $500,000 exempt at FMV $835,000 or less, partial to $860,000) and the newly built home exemption (full to $1,100,000, eliminated at $1,150,000) — confirm the farm/ALR position for a specific parcel; Home Buyers' Plan $60,000; FHSA $40,000 lifetime / $8,000 per year; CMHC premiums 0.6%–4.5%. REDMA s.21 7-day rescission and s.18 trust deposits apply where a presale exists — no presale is verified in this sub-area.

items.t: The pump station is the valley's defining infrastructure: the Salmon River Pump Station has flood box gates that close as Fraser River levels rise, and Council has authorized detailed design and tendering for its upgrades — a live Township project a valley-floor buyer should read before valuing land inside the dykes.

A choice school sits on the upland edge, not in the valley: Coghlan Fundamental Elementary at 4452 256 Street is a district school of choice on the upland east side — and the locator result for that same address is North Otter Elementary / D.W. Poppy Secondary, which is why "the school at the address" and "the catchment for the address" are different questions here.

The only named store near the district is in Fort Langley: Lee's Market, 23320 Mavis Avenue, Fort Langley, is the nearest store named with its address on a Township page — inside the district itself, few or no stores were confirmed, and no recreation centre or library branch inside the district was confirmed either.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Salmon River
Fee-simple parcels

items.t: Valley-floor parcels: farm and acreage houses on large rural lots along the river valley, under the Township Rural Plan designations and Zoning Bylaw No. 2500; the district's farm and acreage homes sit in the rural zones, including RU-2. Lot character as stated: large rural parcels — typical lot sizes from direct Bylaw 2500 text were NOT confirmed, and the RU-2 minimum lot area and frontage were not confirmed from a readable bylaw section: both UNCONFIRMED, no size invented here.

Upland parcels (56 Avenue / Rawlison Crescent side): the same fee-simple acreage form on the upland side of the district — horse owners using the upland lots are part of the typical-buyer picture in the research. No separate upland zone minimum is stated in the research: UNCONFIRMED lot-by-lot.

Strata vs freehold, as stated: most Salmon River properties are non-strata freehold acreages; where a strata parcel exists, BC strata law is the Strata Property Act. (SnapStats FVR September 2026 report.)

ALR vs non-ALR split, as stated: farm land in the valley is in the Agricultural Land Reserve IN PLACES — the research states no percentage split, and none is invented. Confirm a specific parcel on the ALC maps.

Serviced vs unserviced — well/septic ground, as stated: rural properties may use wells — search GWELLS, the provincial database of registered wells and mapped aquifers, for a parcel's record (well reports due within 90 days of constructing, altering or decommissioning a well). No municipal water/sewer position for valley parcels is stated in the research — treat the district as well/septic diligence ground unless the Township confirms otherwise for the parcel.

Flood character of the land itself: the Salmon River valley is Fraser River floodplain land — the Township states the Salmon River Pump Station was originally built to help mitigate flooding of the surrounding agricultural lands during freshet, provides flood protection when Fraser River levels rise, and has flood box gates that close as river levels rise. Valley-floor land value is inseparable from that system.

Riparian character: the Salmon River is salmon-bearing, so setbacks and riparian rules can limit building envelopes near the river — parcel-level setback distances: UNCONFIRMED; check with the Township before planning a build. Price buildable area, not gross area.

items.t: Municipality: Township of Langley, BC — Salmon River is the rural district along the Salmon River in the township's northwest, north of the Otter area and south of Fort Langley.
MLS sub-area name as the board uses it: "Salmon River" (Fraser Valley Real Estate Board data in the SnapStats FVR September 2026 report).
The name is the river's name: the Salmon River is a salmon-bearing watercourse, and Metro Vancouver watershed material covers the Salmon River watershed.
Nearby areas: Fort Langley to the north, Otter District to the south, Walnut Grove to the west, Aldergrove to the southeast.

Main roads and commute: 56 Avenue and Rawlison Crescent on the upland, 232 Street and 240 Street as the north–south edges, and River Road / Glover Road toward Fort Langley; Highway 1 access is south via the 200 Street or 232 Street interchanges; there is no SkyTrain or West Coast Express station in the district.

Schools: catchments are address-based in SD35. For the sample address 4452 256 Street, the SD35 School Locator returns Elementary — North Otter Elementary; Middle — none shown by the locator; Secondary — D.W. Poppy Secondary; other addresses may fall in different catchments, and no home is promised a specific school. Coghlan Fundamental Elementary, 4452 256 Street, a district school of choice, stands on the upland east side; its position inside this board sub-area is not confirmed. No SD35 school physically inside the Salmon River valley itself was confirmed.

Parks/facilities: the Salmon River Natural Area is a Township park listed among the Fort Langley-area parks; no recreation centre or library branch inside the district was confirmed — the nearest Township facilities are in Fort Langley and Walnut Grove.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Salmon River

items.t: Zoning + plans: rural land is under Township of Langley Zoning Bylaw No. 2500 (rural zones, including RU-2; RU-2 minimum lot area/frontage UNCONFIRMED from a readable section; zone assignments for a parcel come from the bylaw Map Schedules through the Township's GeoSource). The Township Official Community Plan and the Rural Plan govern the district.
SSMUH as the Township states it: SSMUH = Bylaw 6020 (adopted November 18, 2024) — NO 6-plex tier in the Township. Suite cap 120 m².

Coach house — fee-simple, never strata (live conflict flagged, not resolved): a coach house is a fee-simple second unit under Zoning Bylaw 2500 s.102 — in s.102 a "coach house" is an accessory dwelling unit located only within the second storey of a detached garage — never a strata unit.

R-CL s.403 (where it applies): 220 m² minimum / 464.5 m² maximum under Zoning Bylaw 2500 s.403 — carried as the Township standing position; R-CL is a Willoughby-form zone and its application to any Salmon River parcel is UNCONFIRMED. Willoughby Plan = Bylaw 1836 (1979), now Schedule 6 to Bylaw 6200 (standing position; Willoughby is a different community — do not apply its plan to Salmon River ground).
Flood / pump-station diligence: Flood status drives insurance and lending on these parcels.

ALR rules (valley farm land in the ALR, in places): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha) — the ALC permits one additional residence without an ALC application where its size rules are met, subject to Township bylaws; BC Assessment farm-class thresholds in full three-tier form ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR.
Federal non-Canadian purchase prohibition — vacant land: Get advice on the current official text for the specific parcel.

faq.q: Are there more or fewer homes for sale in Salmon River than in June?
faq.a: In Salmon River, listings of houses rose from 20 in June to 22 in September (+10.0%); condos and townhomes rose from 3 in June to 4 in September (+33.3%).

faq.q: How big is Salmon River compared with the rest of Langley?
faq.a: In September 2026, Salmon River held 4.9% of the 449 houses listed in Langley and 0.6% of the 699 condos and townhomes listed in Langley.

faq.q: How many homes sold in Salmon River from June to September 2026?
faq.a: 17 houses and 1 condos and townhomes sold in Salmon River over those 4 months.

faq.q: How do I find out which school serves an address in Salmon River?
faq.a: School catchments are set by address, so use the school district's catchment locator with the exact address. Catchment lines change, so check before you write an offer.

faq.q: Who can help me buy or sell in Salmon River?
faq.a: Jared Gibbons, REALTOR® with Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, works across the Fraser Valley and Metro Vancouver. Call or text 604-928-1361 or use the contact form on this site.

faq.q: Could a condo building be built on the valley farm land?
faq.a: Not as-of-right on ALR land: a strata plan causes a subdivision under ALC Information Bulletin 09, s. 6, and subdivision of agricultural land requires Commission permission after an application or a permission in the ALR General Regulation. Whether any specific parcel could obtain that permission is UNCONFIRMED — it is an application outcome, not a published rule.

faq.q: Is a Salmon River acreage with a suite a "condo alternative"?
faq.a: It is a different legal thing: the Township states lots over 4,050 m² may add one secondary suite (capped at 120 m²) or one accessory dwelling unit depending on zoning, and on ALR land the additional-residence size caps are 90 m² (40 ha or less) or 186 m² (over 40 ha). A suite is part of one freehold title, not a strata lot — there is no Form B, no strata fee and no strata corporation.

faq.q: A listing says "strata" for a Salmon River property. What should I check?
faq.a: If it is a strata lot, request the Form B; the strata must provide it within 7 days.

faq.q: Does the flood picture matter more here than condo rules?
faq.a: Yes. The valley is Fraser River floodplain land; the Township states the Salmon River Pump Station provides flood protection when Fraser River levels rise and was built to mitigate flooding of the surrounding agricultural lands during freshet, and upgrades are in detailed design and tendering.

faq.q: Which schools serve a Salmon River address?
faq.a: For the sample address 4452 256 Street, the SD35 School Locator returns North Otter Elementary and D.W. Poppy Secondary, with no middle school shown; Coghlan Fundamental Elementary at that address is a district school of choice on the upland east side, and the guide page also names Peterson Road Elementary. Run the exact address — catchments are address-based, and no school sits inside the valley itself on the sources checked.

faq.q: Are there any townhouses in Salmon River?
faq.a: The stock is freehold acreage houses; the nearest townhouse stock is in Fort Langley, Walnut Grove and Willoughby.

faq.q: Can I stratify a big farmhouse into townhouse units?
faq.a: Not on ALR land: an ALR residence cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)), and subdivision of ALR land needs Commission permission. Confirm the parcel's ALR status on the ALC maps first.

faq.q: Can an acreage add a second dwelling?
faq.a: On ALR land the ALC permits one additional residence without an application at up to 90 m² (40 ha or less) or 186 m² (over 40 ha), subject to Township bylaws; the Township's SSMUH rules also allow a suite or accessory unit on lots over 4,050 m² depending on zoning, and a coach house in the Township is a fee-simple second unit under Bylaw 2500 s.102 — never a strata townhouse.
